prompt: Candid documentary photo of a real serving of babi guling as eaten at a small Balinese warung in Ubud. CRUCIAL defining feature — the CRACKLING: blistered, puffed, bubbly golden-brown crackle armor from spit-roasting a young pig over a coconut-husk fire for hours. The crackle surface must be visibly bubbled and blistered, with raised crispy bubbles 2-10mm across and a heavily cratered, almost coral-like surface — NOT smooth, NOT glazed, NOT fried-battered, NOT thin fried coating. Show 2-3 pieces of pork with the bubbly crackle cap prominent and unmistakable on each. Served on a banana leaf (authentic Balinese presentation). Side: small mound of white rice, tiny saucer of sambal matah (raw shallot + chili + lime + lemongrass), small heap of lawar (chopped pork with grated coconut + long bean + herbs), wedge of lime. Worn wooden or formica warung table. Glass of es teh and clay periuk pot in soft background. Soft natural Balinese daylight from the open shopfront, ~40° above, 35mm lens, moderate depth of field. Everyday unstyled, slightly messy crumb of crackle on the banana leaf. The bubbly crackle is the visual hero. Do NOT render as: babi kecap, babi goreng kremes, babi panggang, or fried chicken. No microgreens, no fusion garnish, no studio lighting, no text, no logos, no people, no hands.
